summary: Attacked the Group theory area: the Tau Ceti roadmaps CFSGStatement (9 layers) and ProfiniteProPGroups (12 layers). One finding, medium: Layer 3 of ProfiniteProPGroups cites a Mathlib prerequisite, `IsPGroup.exists_maximal_subgroup_normal`, that does not exist at the pinned commit, though the mathematics is reachable by composing three named Mathlib results. Nothing else broke. The area is unusually well coordinated: both of the overlaps that looked like duplication are settled in the sources themselves, with CFSG Layer 0 saying 'Consume, rather than duplicate' and naming ReductiveGroups Layer 9, and ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 6 saying 'this roadmap defines no second cohomological dimension' and deferring to ProfiniteCohomology. Library coverage for all 21 layers is recorded from two accepted audits, the one Part II routed here has a conforming title, and the remaining overlap is already resolved by RS-29.
checked: Both roadmaps in full: CFSGStatement's 9 stages and ProfiniteProPGroups's 12, with their documents. The two stages that share the key 'Layer 9' are deliberate, not a numbering collision: the README carries '### Layer 9 prerequisites: two owned inputs' and '### Layer 9: the classification of Demushkin groups' as separate headings, and the first says its inputs are 'built here, before the classification'.

Every Mathlib declaration the two roadmaps cite with their `M` prefix: 42 names in ProfiniteProPGroups, of which 41 resolve at the pin and one does not, which is the finding; CFSGStatement cites none in that form. Every relative roadmap link in the two documents resolves to an existing roadmap document.

The two apparent duplications, read in the sources rather than inferred, and both are explicit coordination. CFSGStatement Layer 0 and ReductiveGroups Layer 9 both concern pinned Chevalley-Demazure groups, and they name each other: Layer 0 says 'Consume, rather than duplicate: ... reductive algebraic groups, whose Layer 9 gives pinned Chevalley-Demazure group schemes over ℤ, base change, points, and root subgroups', while Layer 9 says 'It exists because a downstream consumer needs it ...: the CFSG statement roadmap'. ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 6 and ProfiniteCohomology Layer 11 both concern cohomological dimension, and Layer 6 opens '`cd_p G` is `ProfiniteCohomology.cd_p p G` ... That declaration belongs to the Profinite Cohomology roadmap, and this roadmap defines no second cohomological dimension', citing rather than restating the two reduction theorems and owning only the pro-p devissage.

Whether that second dependency is recorded anywhere machine-readable: it is, in the ProfiniteProPGroups link map, as ProfiniteCohomology layer-11-cohomological-dimension -> ProfiniteProPGroups layer-6-cohomological-dimension-of-pro-p-groups, alongside seventeen other links from ProfiniteCohomology into this roadmap.

The remaining concept-level overlaps, swept across every roadmap in the atlas: groups of Lie type, sporadic groups, profinite groups, Demushkin groups, free pro-p groups, supernatural numbers, the embedding problem and profinite Sylow theory. Supernatural numbers and free pro-p groups occur in no other roadmap. The embedding-problem overlap with InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.4 is already resolved by RS-29, whose owners move the generic finite embedding problem and continuous weak solution to ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 5. The Demushkin mentions elsewhere are consumers in ClassFieldTheory and LocalFieldsRamification, not plans.

Library coverage and the atlas record. All 21 layers of the two roadmaps have entries in data/library-coverage.json, from AUDIT-21 and AUDIT-22, both with accepted reviews, verdicts ranging over built, partly built and not built. The layers' atlas `status` is 'unknown' and their `requires` lists are empty, but neither is a defect of this area: across the atlas every one of the 656 upstream stages carries status 'unknown' and every one of the 1306 campaign stages carries 'needs_source_decomposition', so the field records no build state anywhere, and only 4 of 656 upstream stages populate `requires` against 1289 of 1306 campaign stages, so the empty list is the upstream convention, prerequisites being stated in the layer prose instead.

What the area plans against what the libraries have. Demushkin groups and cohomological dimension have zero declarations at the pin and are correctly planned; supernatural numbers, profinite foundations, Sylow theory and the Frattini subgroup exist in Tau Ceti and Mathlib and are correctly recorded as built or partly built by the two audits.

The one paper routed to the area, PAPER-BRESCIANI-24, which proposes ProfiniteProPGroupsPartIISplitCompletion with 7 items. Its title, 'Profinite and pro-p groups, Part II: exactness of completion for split extensions', is an exact prefix extension of the parent's atlas title as section 15 requires, and the roadmap id is free.

The three restructuring proposals that name the area. RS-05, RS-16 and RS-29 mention ProfiniteProPGroups; none narrows, keeps or drops any of its layers. RS-16's owner entry, which assigns 'Completed Z_p group algebra of a profinite group, compact actions and procyclic/dyadic coordinates' to Layer 9 prerequisites, is accurate: that layer's subsection 'The completed group algebra of the orientation image' defines `completedGroupAlgebra p Γ := lim_U ℤ_p[Γ/U]` for a general profinite Γ with its compact topological algebra package, and treats both the procyclic and the dyadic C₂ × ℤ₂ shapes.

findings.where: tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteProPGroups, Layer 3 (the maximal pro-p quotient and the Frattini subgroup), its *Needs:* line — content/tau-ceti/ProfiniteProPGroups/README.md line 326
findings.claim: Layer 3 names a Mathlib declaration that does not exist at the pinned commit. Its prerequisite line reads '*Needs:* M `frattini`, M `IsPGroup.exists_maximal_subgroup_normal` and the finite Frattini lemmas', where the roadmap's `M` prefix means Mathlib supplies it. `frattini` does; `IsPGroup.exists_maximal_subgroup_normal` does not, under that name or any other I could find. The mathematics — every maximal subgroup of a finite p-group is normal — is in Mathlib, but only by composing three separately named results, so a builder who follows the line as written looks for one declaration and finds nothing.
findings.evidence: At Mathlib 082e2d3 the declarations index has no `IsPGroup.exists_maximal_subgroup_normal`; the complete list of `IsPGroup.*` declarations contains nothing about maximal subgroups or normality beyond the sup/inf lemmas `to_sup_of_normal_left`, `to_sup_of_normal_right` and their primed forms. Mathlib/GroupTheory/PGroup.lean contains no such theorem. Mathlib's whole Frattini API is six declarations in Mathlib/GroupTheory/Frattini.lean — `frattini` (line 24), `frattini_le_coatom` (29), `frattini_le_comap_frattini_of_surjective` (34), `frattini_characteristic` (42), `frattini_nongenerating` (53) and `frattini_nilpotent` (58) — and none of them is the normality statement. The other 41 Mathlib names this roadmap cites with the `M` prefix all resolve at the pin, so the convention is used correctly everywhere else and this is a single wrong name rather than a misunderstanding. The content is available: `IsPGroup.isNilpotent` (Mathlib/GroupTheory/Nilpotent.lean:1247), `Group.normalizerCondition_of_isNilpotent` (Mathlib/GroupTheory/Nilpotent.lean:1201) and `Subgroup.NormalizerCondition.normal_of_coatom` (Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Subgroup/Order.lean:47), the last carrying the docstring 'In a group that satisfies the normalizer condition, every maximal subgroup is normal'.
findings.fix: Replace the single name in Layer 3's *Needs:* line with the route that exists, as a note for the Tau Ceti maintainer since the roadmap is upstream: '*Needs:* M `frattini`, M `IsPGroup.isNilpotent`, M `Group.normalizerCondition_of_isNilpotent`, M `Subgroup.NormalizerCondition.normal_of_coatom` and the finite Frattini lemmas'. Nothing about the layer's own targets changes — the index-p Frattini characterisation, `proPFrattini` and the elementary-abelian quotient are unaffected; only the prerequisite is renamed to something a builder can open. If the maintainer would rather have one lemma to cite, the composite 'a maximal subgroup of a finite p-group is normal' is a two-line consequence of those three and could be contributed upstream under the cited name.
